content: For social media text corpus (FSD and Twitter), a named entity tagger specifically built for Twitter is used to extract named entities including locations from tweets. A Twitter Part-of-Speech (POS) tagger BIBREF15 is used for POS tagging and only words tagged with nouns, verbs and adjectives are retained as keywords. For the Google dataset, we use the Stanford Named Entity Recognizer to identify the named entities (organization, location and person). Due to the `date' information not being provided in the Google dataset, we further divide the non-location named entities into two categories (`person' and `organization') and employ a quadruple <organization, location, person, keyword> to denote an event in news articles. We also remove common stopwords and only keep the recognized named entities and the tokens which are verbs, nouns or adjectives.
